topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture series on cancer causes, outlines the core biological concepts to be covered, and sets the learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer Evolution and the Sources of Mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary disease driven by genetic mutations and the microenvironment, outlining the endogenous, inherited, and environmental origins of these mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures and Epidemiological Evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine common environmental carcinogen exposures, public perceptions of intrinsic cancer risk, and global epidemiological evidence demonstrating environmental influences on cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents in Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how pathogens contribute to malignancy through mechanisms such as chronic inflammation and oncogene activation, highlighted by the case study of Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Biochemical Mechanisms of Chemical and Physical Mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular mechanisms by which dietary, environmental, and chemical carcinogens damage DNA, including metabolic activation, adduct formation, and oxidative stress.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Host Susceptibility, and Mechanistic Principles
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss how non-mutagenic promoters, chronic inflammation, and host developmental stages cooperate with initiating mutations, concluding with a summary of carcinogenic principles.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Testing Carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the experimental and investigative techniques used to assess carcinogenicity, including mutational signature sequencing, epidemiology, animal bioassays, and in vitro tests.

topics.label: Summary and Risk-Benefit Considerations
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture by summarising the environmental basis of cancer and the practical considerations of assessing exposure risks against benefits.
